label: Individuals sentenced (USSC)
description: Number of individual offenders sentenced in the district in the fiscal year and reported to the U.S. Sentencing Commission (records in the USSC Individual Offender datafile; before FY2018 the USSC called these 'guideline cases'). Organizational defendants, resentencings and appeals are not included.
caveats: Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.
FY1995-FY2001 values are the district totals printed in the USSC Statistical Information Packet (Table 1 note); FY2002+ are counts of datafile records, which reproduce the packet totals exactly.

FY1995-FY1999 values are as printed in each district's own packet; summed over districts they do not always equal the national packet figure (FY1999 imprisonment N: districts exceed the nation by 57 with all 94 present; other years have missing district-years). Do not present FY1995-FY1999 district counts as adding up to the nation; see packet_reconciliation.csv. FY2000+ add up exactly.
formula: count of datafile records with DISTRICT = d

label: Cases with guideline range comparison
description: Denominator of the guideline-range percentages: individuals whose sentence the USSC could compare with the guideline range.
caveats: Era-specific USSC exclusions (missing departure information before FY2005; missing documents or no applicable guideline afterwards).
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.
formula: count of cases with non-missing range category

derived_formula_by_basis.pooled_published_halves: N_first_half + N_second_half (FY2004 pre/post-Blakely, FY2005 pre/post-Booker half-year tables)

label: Sentenced within the guideline range
description: Share of individuals sentenced within the applicable federal sentencing guideline range. Denominator: individuals whose sentence could be compared with the guideline range (USSC excludes cases with missing or indeterminable guideline information and offenses with no applicable guideline) = ussc_cases_range_known.
caveats: Before Booker (FY1995-FY2004 and the first 3.5 months of FY2005) the guidelines were mandatory and 'within range' means no departure was granted (packet departure table); from FY2006 (BOOKERCD=0) and FY2018 (SENTRNGE=0) it is the USSC's 'Within Guideline Range' category. The USSC's FY2025 Sourcebook Figure 9 shows the FY2018 methodology change did not alter the within-range share (FY2017: 49.1% under both methods).
FY2004 and FY2005 are pooled from the two half-year tables the USSC published (pre/post-Blakely; pre/post-Booker); each half was validated separately.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.
higher_means: more sentences inside the guideline range

breaks.note: United States v. Booker (Jan 12, 2005) made the guidelines advisory
USSC adopted SENTRNGE methodology; within-range share unaffected

derived_formula_by_basis.pooled_published_halves: 100 * (n_first_half + n_second_half) / (N_first_half + N_second_half): the full fiscal year pooled from the two half-year tables the USSC printed (FY2004 pre/post-Blakely, FY2005 pre/post-Booker)

label: §5K1.1 substantial-assistance departures
description: Share of individuals who received a downward departure on a government motion under USSG §5K1.1 for substantial assistance to authorities (USSC category 'Substantial Assistance Departure' / '§5K1.1 Substantial Assistance'). Denominator: individuals whose sentence could be compared with the guideline range (USSC excludes cases with missing or indeterminable guideline information and offenses with no applicable guideline) = ussc_cases_range_known.
caveats: FY2002: DEPART codes 3,5,7,9 (any §5K1.1); FY2003 DEPART_D=0; FY2004-FY2005 DEPART_A=2; FY2005 post-Booker-FY2017 BOOKERCD=5; FY2018+ SENTRNGE=2. Cases with both §5K1.1 and other departures are counted as §5K1.1, as the USSC does.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.

derived_formula_by_basis.pooled_published_halves: 100 * (n_first_half + n_second_half) / (N_first_half + N_second_half): the full fiscal year pooled from the two half-year tables the USSC printed (FY2004 pre/post-Blakely, FY2005 pre/post-Booker)

label: §5K3.1 early-disposition (fast-track) departures
description: Share of individuals who received a downward departure under USSG §5K3.1 (early disposition / 'fast-track' programs authorized by the Attorney General). Denominator: individuals whose sentence could be compared with the guideline range (USSC excludes cases with missing or indeterminable guideline information and offenses with no applicable guideline) = ussc_cases_range_known.
caveats: Published separately by district from FY2006 (FY2003-FY2005 packets fold it into 'government initiated departure'). Most districts have no program, so 0.0 is common and real.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.

label: Sentenced above the guideline range
description: Share of individuals in the sentenced above the guideline range category: USSC 'Cases sentenced above guideline range' (upward departures, upward departures with Booker/§3553, above range with Booker/§3553, remaining above range; BOOKERCD 1-4). Denominator: individuals whose sentence could be compared with the guideline range (USSC excludes cases with missing or indeterminable guideline information and offenses with no applicable guideline) = ussc_cases_range_known.
caveats: Only FY2006-FY2017, the years the USSC itself published this four-way grouping (packet Table 8 'Comparison of sentence imposed and position relative to the guideline range'). FY2005 is split pre/post-Booker and FY1995-FY2004 used departure categories only; from FY2018 the USSC reports departures and variances instead (see the ussc_pct_above_range_2018scheme variable). These years are omitted, not imputed.

In FY2006-FY2009 packets the group percentage was printed as the sum of rounded sub-category percentages; this value is count/denominator (counts match exactly), so it can differ from the printed figure by up to 0.2 points.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.

label: Sentenced above the guideline range (FY2018 methodology)
description: DERIVED: sum of USSC SENTRNGE categories: Upward Departure + Upward Variance (SENTRNGE 1, 6), as a share of cases with a guideline-range comparison under the FY2018 methodology (n_basis column). Government/non-government attribution uses the USSC's own test (the prosecution initiated, proposed or stipulated to the sentence).
caveats: Derived by this lane: the USSC publishes each component (packet Table 8, FY2018+) but not this sum.

FY2014-FY2017 values come from the USSC's supplemental datafiles, which carry the FY2018-methodology variable SENTRNGE for those years (joined to the main datafile on USSCIDN to get the district); the USSC released them so researchers can apply the current methodology to FY2014+, but did not publish district tables for those years on this basis. FY2018+ values reproduce the packet tables.

Kept separate from the FY2006-FY2017 id without the suffix (BOOKERCD scheme, as published) because the USSC stopped printing this grouping after FY2017. For FY2014-FY2017 both were computed and are IDENTICAL for every district and year (tested): the FY2018 methodology change re-labelled departures vs variances without moving any case between these four groups.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.
formula: 100 * (Upward Departure + Upward Variance (SENTRNGE 1, 6)) / cases with SENTRNGE non-missing

label: Sentenced to prison
description: Share of individuals sentenced to a term of imprisonment (prison only, or prison plus alternative confinement / split sentence; SENTIMP 1-2), among individuals with sentence-type information, fine-only sentences included in the denominator (USSC FY2018+ packet Table 5 convention, applied to every year).
caveats: FY2002-FY2017 packets left fine-only cases out of the sentence-type denominator; this variable keeps them in for every year so the series is consistent. The numerators (prison counts) match the packets exactly in every year.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.

derived_formula_by_basis.computed_ussc_definition: 100 * (prison_only + prison_with_alternatives) / cases_with_sentence_type, computed by this lane from the USSC Individual Offender datafile with the USSC's own definition, in a year when the USSC did not print this statistic

label: Average sentence (months)
description: Mean sentence length in months under the USSC's FY2018+ convention: imprisonment plus months of alternative confinement, probation-only and fine-only sentences counted as 0 months, terms over 470 months set to 469.99 (life = 470). Variable SENSPCAP (FY2018+); for FY2002-FY2017 the identical rule applied to SENSPLT0.
caveats: FY2018-FY2025 reproduce packet Table 7 'Sentence length'. FY2002-FY2017 are computed by this lane with the same rule; the USSC's own packets for those years published only the length of imprisonment (see ussc_mean_prison_months).

Cases with no sentence-length value (SENSPLT0/SENSPCAP missing: 746 records nationally in FY2002, falling to 0-2 a year from FY2017) are left out of the mean, the median and N (n_basis), as the USSC leaves out a missing SENSPCAP. Before 2026-11-27 this lane wrongly counted them as 469.99 months in FY2002-FY2017 (statistics audit, blocker 1); corrected.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.
formula: mean(min(SENSPCAP or SENSPLT0, 469.99; life = 470)) over cases with a non-missing value

derived_formula_by_basis.computed_ussc_definition: mean(min(SENSPCAP or SENSPLT0, 469.99; life = 470)) over cases with a non-missing value, computed by this lane from the USSC Individual Offender datafile with the USSC's own definition, in a year when the USSC did not print this statistic

label: Median sentence (months)
description: Median of the same quantity as ussc_mean_sentence_months (probation = 0; terms over 470 months set to 469.99, life = 470).
caveats: As for ussc_mean_sentence_months. The median is 0 where more than half the individuals received no confinement.
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.
formula: median(min(SENSPCAP or SENSPLT0, 469.99; life = 470)) over cases with a non-missing value

derived_formula_by_basis.computed_ussc_definition: median(min(SENSPCAP or SENSPLT0, 469.99; life = 470)) over cases with a non-missing value, computed by this lane from the USSC Individual Offender datafile with the USSC's own definition, in a year when the USSC did not print this statistic

caveats: FY1995-FY2001 are the published packet values; FY2002-FY2017 reproduce the packets; FY2018-FY2025 are computed by this lane with the same rule (the USSC switched to the probation-as-zero convention, see ussc_mean_sentence_months).
Territorial courts (D. Guam, D.N. Mar. I., D.V.I.) and some small districts have few cases; see ussc_cases_total and the n_basis column before comparing percentages.

derived_formula_by_basis.computed_ussc_definition: mean(SENTTOT | SENTTOT > 0), computed by this lane from the USSC Individual Offender datafile with the USSC's own definition, in a year when the USSC did not print this statistic

label: Cases with a primary offense type
description: Denominator of the offense-mix shares: individuals with a known primary offense type.
caveats: Primary offense type is the variable the USSC used in that year's own Sourcebook and packets: OFFTYPE2 (FY1995-FY2009) and OFFTYPSB (FY2010-FY2017), both assigned from the count of conviction with the highest statutory maximum; OFFGUIDE (FY2018+), assigned mainly from the primary sentencing guideline the court applied. The FY2018 change of basis is a definitional break for every offense category; the USSC uses the same category names on both sides of it for drug trafficking, immigration, firearms and child pornography.

FY1995-FY1999 values are as printed in each district's own packet; summed over districts they do not always equal the national packet figure (FY1999 imprisonment N: districts exceed the nation by 57 with all 94 present; other years have missing district-years). Do not present FY1995-FY1999 district counts as adding up to the nation; see packet_reconciliation.csv. FY2000+ add up exactly.
